The residual plot shows a second pattern as well: the spread of the residuals increases with predicted ridership, and the errors are not symmetric (a few very large positive residuals at high ridership). Because ridership is right-skewed and the effects of population and jobs are probably multiplicative rather than additive, a linear model in levels is a poor fit. The model also predicts negative ridership for 0 station(s), which is impossible. The standard errors and p-values from Question 9 are therefore unreliable, because they assume constant error variance.
